report.headline: The OCEAN(a) outcomes trial of olpasiran cannot be forecast due to insufficient data; enrollment is complete but the event count and on-treatment Lp(a) reduction at the phase 3 dose are unknown.
report.summary: The phase 3 OCEAN(a) trial randomized 7,297 patients with Lp(a) ≥200 nmol/L to olpasiran or placebo, with a primary endpoint of time to CHD death, myocardial infarction, or urgent coronary revascularization over a planned 5-year median follow-up (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05581303). Human genetics strongly support Lp(a) as causal for coronary disease (Open Targets LPA score 0.922; Mendelian randomization odds ratios 1.8–3.67) (opentargets:LPA; Genetic variants associated with Lp(a) lipoprotein level and coronary disease). Phase 2 data show potent but waning Lp(a) reduction: −97.4% at week 36 declining to −27.9% at week 96 for the 75 mg Q12W dose (Small Interfering RNA to Reduce Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease; The Off-Treatment Effects of Olpasiran on Lipoprotein(a) Lowering: OCEAN(a)-DOSE Extension Period Results). The phase 3 dose regimen is not confirmed in verified facts, and no placebo-adjusted phase 3 biomarker change is available. The calculator estimates an expected hazard ratio of 0.82 (18% relative risk reduction) but requires 796 events for 80% power; the actual event count is unknown because the trial has not read out (calculator). The forecast is therefore 'not_computable' with medium confidence, driven primarily by missing event and biomarker data rather than a demonstrated small treatment effect.
key_evidence: Primary endpoint: time to CHD death, MI, or urgent coronary revascularization; ~5 years median follow-up (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05581303)

Phase 2 biomarker effect wanes from −97.4% at week 36 to −27.9% at week 96 for 75 mg Q12W dose (Small Interfering RNA to Reduce Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease; The Off-Treatment Effects of Olpasiran on Lipoprotein(a) Lowering: OCEAN(a)-DOSE Extension Period Results)

Genetic evidence: Open Targets LPA score 0.922; Mendelian randomization ORs 1.8–3.67 for coronary disease (opentargets:LPA; Genetic variants associated with Lp(a) lipoprotein level and coronary disease)
Calculator output: expected HR 0.82, causal RRR 18%, category insufficient_data, weakest link trial size (events) unknown; 796 events needed for 80% power (calculator)
report.what_would_change_this: A placebo-adjusted Lp(a) reduction from phase 3 at the trial dose and background therapy, together with the total events accrued and observed hazard ratio with confidence interval at primary analysis.
report.readthrough_note: Other Lp(a)-lowering programmes in outcomes trials include pelacarsen (Lp(a) antisense, HORIZON trial) and lepodisiran (LPA siRNA); their readouts will inform whether sustained Lp(a) reduction translates to cardiovascular benefit in high-Lp(a) populations.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: LPA genetic association score 0.922 with coronary artery disease (Open Targets), with 183 evidence items and 8 studies published before cutoff (GCST010479, FINNGEN_R12_I9_UAP, GCST90436075, GCST008370, GCST90013864, etc.). Score well above 0.5 threshold with coronary disease studies.

changes.method: Placebo-adjusted percent change at week 36 from phase 2 OCEAN(a)-DOSE (75 mg Q12W dose); baseline derived from phase 3 OCEAN(a) Outcomes Trial entry threshold (200 nmol/L = 83.3 mg/dL using 2.4 nmol/L = 1 mg/dL conversion)

mechanism.notes: Phase 3 dose not confirmed in verified facts; calculator uses phase 2 75 mg Q12W week 36 data (-97.4%) as best available proxy. Lp(a) reduction wanes substantially over time (week 60: -76.2%, week 72: -53.0%, week 84: -44.0%, week 96: -27.9% per f_8f280782644c42, f_8f049f03cf46be, f_7a3285f171f2ca, f_46b0c66e023873). Baseline uses phase 3 entry threshold (200 nmol/L = 83.3 mg/dL) as lower bound since phase 3 measured baseline not available. Phase 2 baseline was 260.3 nmol/L (108.5 mg/dL) with 150 nmol/L entry threshold. No LDL-C or apoB changes reported for olpasiran. Trial enrollment complete (7,297 randomized per f_227a384ed5a465) but follow-up ongoing; no readout yet.

hypotheses.would_settle: Trial readout with event counts, HR, and on-treatment Lp(a) trajectory; confirmation of phase 3 dose regimen

issues.issue: Calculator baseline (83.3 mg/dL) derived from phase 3 entry threshold (≥200 nmol/L) rather than measured mean baseline; phase 2 median baseline was 260.3 nmol/L (108.5 mg/dL). Actual phase 3 mean baseline likely higher, making the LDL-equivalent (0.799 mmol/L) and expected HR (0.82) conservative. The population hypothesis notes this but the calculator input should flag the assumption more explicitly.
issues.request: Add a note to calculator input assumptions that baseline is a lower-bound estimate from entry threshold; true mean baseline unknown but phase 2 median was 108.5 mg/dL.

issues.issue: Substantial biomarker waning in phase 2 extension: -97.4% at week 36 → -27.9% at week 96 (75 mg Q12W). Calculator uses week 36 value with time_factor=1.0 for a 5-year (260-week) trial, overstating sustained effect. This is the strongest driver of effect_too_small risk.
issues.request: Document in calculator assumptions that time_factor=1.0 does not capture waning; average on-treatment effect over 5 years likely far lower than week 36 snapshot.

issues.issue: Phase 3 dose regimen not confirmed in verified facts. Calculator uses phase 2 75 mg Q12W data as proxy. Hypotheses (insufficient_data, effect_too_small) correctly flag this, but no verified fact establishes the phase 3 dose.
issues.request: Search for phase 3 protocol publications, registry amendments, or sponsor disclosures confirming olpasiran dose and dosing interval in NCT05581303.

issues.issue: execution_or_nonscientific hypothesis claims 'No conduct issues or early stopping reported in registry' citing f_227a384ed5a465, but that fact only reports n_randomized=7297. The registry record (ctgov:NCT05581303) would need to be checked for conduct issues; the citation does not directly support the claim.
issues.request: Verify NCT05581303 registry history for any protocol amendments, enrollment pauses, or safety holds; update reference or remove claim if unsupported.

issues.issue: effect_too_small against point 'Genetic calibration suggests larger effect possible per unit Lp(a) lowering' cites only f_bbddc6c5c50370 (genetic association score 0.922). The MR studies (f_4acadea0e413c9, f_9efe57c23c1f23, f_d944124729f464, f_d954b811762c1a) provide direct effect-size estimates per Lp(a) increase and are better evidence for this claim.
issues.request: Update reference list for that against point to include the MR study facts.
